title: Bizzare behavour of uptime graph in system monitor widget
line: System Monitor charts of time sensors like Uptime show correct values on the side axis instead of 0:00:00.
explanation: The chart's axis labels hand their values to the formatter as strings, and the in-between ones are fractional ("47377.75"). The time and ticks formatters converted them with toLongLong(), which fails on a decimal string and returns 0, so every label except a whole-number top value read 0:00:00 (and flickered when the top value was fractional too). The formatters now read the value as a double and round it.

commits.message:
formatter: Format fractional time values instead of showing zero

Chart axis labels pass values as strings such as "47377.75", and the
time and ticks formatters read them with toLongLong(), which fails for
those strings and showed 0:00:00. Read them as doubles and round instead.

BUG: 521258

media.caption: Line chart of Uptime on master: three of four axis labels read 0:00:00

review.text: Solid, targeted fix in libksysguard's Formatter.cpp that parses time and ticks values via qRound64(value.toDouble()) instead of value.toLongLong(), matching formatNumber() and formatBootTimestamp() in the same file. This directly fixes the root cause where fractional chart axis label strings like "47377.75" failed toLongLong() conversion and displayed as 0:00:00, passes formatter tests, and is clearly verified by the before/after screenshots.

reviews.text: Solid, targeted fix in libksysguard's Formatter.cpp that parses time and ticks values via qRound64(value.toDouble()) instead of value.toLongLong(), matching formatNumber() and formatBootTimestamp() in the same file. This directly fixes the root cause where fractional chart axis label strings like "47377.75" failed toLongLong() conversion and displayed as 0:00:00, passes formatter tests, and is clearly verified by the before/after screenshots.

Root cause confirmed in code: KQuickCharts' AxisLabels attached label is a QString, and formatTime/formatTicks used QVariant::toLongLong(), which returns 0 for decimal strings like "47377.75", so the intermediate axis labels (and the top one whenever it was fractional) read 0:00:00, which is exactly the reporter's flicker to and from 0. Reading as double and rounding fixes it in the shared formatter, harmless for integer inputs and well within double precision for uptime/ticks. The after shot shows evenly spaced correct durations; the flat block dropping to 0 is the normal history fill, as in CPU charts. Minimal, accurate commit with BUG: 521258.
